name: Alpha Mask
description: Makes parts of the base image see-through based on the brightness of the mask image. Black mask pixels keep the base fully visible, white pixels hide it completely, grays fade it partially and fully transparent mask pixels hide it as well. The mask is read pixel by pixel at the same coordinates as the base, so it should have the same size as the base texture. A set of masks with a growing white area, combined with a variable, gives a dissolve or build-up effect.

fields.description: The location of the mask texture. Can use variables.

name: Color
description: Paints a color over the base image, keeping its transparency. Unlike Tint, which multiplies and can only make pixels darker, this mixes every pixel towards the color, so it also works on dark textures and can brighten them. At an opacity of 1 every pixel becomes the exact color, lower values blend it with the original. Both settings can use variables, with the same note about generated textures as Tint.

fields.description: The color as hex, like "ffd24a" or "#ffd24a". Can use variables.
How much of the color is mixed in, from 0 (no change) to 1 (only the color). Can use variables.
Only pixels with exactly this color (as hex, like "ff0000") are recolored, every other pixel stays untouched. Can use variables.

name: Overlay
description: Draws a second image on top of the base image, respecting its transparency, like stacking two layers in an image editor. The overlay is read pixel by pixel at the same coordinates as the base, so it should have the same size as the base texture.

fields.description: The location of the overlay texture. Can use variables.
If true, the overlay is only applied where the base already has pixels, so it can never add pixels outside the existing shape.

name: Tint
description: Multiplies the colors of the base image with a color, keeping its transparency, so one grayscale or neutral texture can be recolored. Both settings can use variables, which makes the color and strength follow a data attachment. Note that variable values also end up in the generated texture's path, so a color variable should be lowercase hex without a leading #, and a strength variable should take only a few different values (for example integer percentages mapped in a Value), because every distinct value creates its own texture.

fields.description: The tint color as hex, like "ffd24a" or "#ffd24a". Can use variables.
How strongly the tint is applied, from 0 (no change) to 1 (full tint). Can use variables.
Only pixels with exactly this color (as hex, like "ff0000") are tinted, every other pixel stays untouched. Useful to recolor just one part of a texture. Can use variables.
